notes: C1 grammar as executable expectations. A relay's parser must map each input to the expected outcome. 'correction' means an immediate in-thread correction (never a modal) and NO domain event to the service. 'not_a_pull' means the message is ordinary channel traffic. The keyword is the exact token 'pull:' at message start (v1 reads the spec literally; kaizen-open).

expect.sentence: the build is red on main

expect.sentence: the review has sat two days with no ack

expect.sentence: the deploy needs three manual steps

expect.sentence: I cannot tell which error state this AC covers

grammar_cases.name: invalid class gets an in-thread correction, never a modal, no event

identical_event_rule.notes: C1: the optional /pull adapter and the canonical text grammar produce the IDENTICAL domain event, thread, and log entry. Usage is never compared by input method. A conforming relay must produce byte-equal domain events from both inputs across the full equality scope — matching only class and sentence does not conform.

equality.notes: Every field of the POSTed domain event (puller, class, sentence, origin tokens) must be equal between the two inputs; only the per-delivery identity (event_id) and timestamp may differ. The relay must also target the same thread for both.
